title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-samir
content:
SUMMARY: - High-level: notes and breadcrumbs from debugging the smart-routing fallback + regional failover incident on 2026-02-28. This is my scratchpad: commands I ran, error snippets I captured, hypotheses I considered, and the mitigation steps we applied. - Affected surface: hosted API requests routed from us-west-2 that got served from a fallback model variant in us-east-1; high 5xx rate and increased latency for a 30m window. TIMELINE (local timestamps UTC-8): - 2026-02-28 14:03: first alert from PagerDuty (route: /v1/generate, error rate spike from 0.2% -> 8%). - 2026-02-28 14:05: slack thread created #inc-smart-routing (link above). - 2026-02-28 14:07: confirmed elevated 5xx specifically for us-west-2 origin traffic. - 2026-02-28 14:12: reproduced locally with curl against edge endpoint, saw 504 / "No healthy hosts for route". - 2026-02-28 14:20: implemented manual change to fallback policy (temporary prefer-local fallback) and restarted route-manager pods. - 2026-02-28 14:30: 5xx rate dropped to ~0.6% and latency improved; incident declared mitigated at ~14:42. OBSERVED SYMPTOMS / METRICS: - sudden increase in 502/504 errors for requests coming from us-west-2 edge nodes. - routing controller logs show repeated healthcheck failures against model-serving backends in us-west-2. - Smart-routing decision engine logged fallback decisions to model-variant "redwood-small-v1@us-east-1" (we saw more cross-region fallbacks than usual). - Console traces show spike in "route-lookup" latency and "backend-connect-timeout" errors. KEY LOG SNIPPETS (sanitized): - router-be-3 (2026-02-28T22:11:32Z): ERROR backend-healthcheck: "HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable" to /health (200 expected) for backend ip=10.20.5.12 - route-manager (2026-02-28T22:12:01Z): WARN smart-routing: "no healthy hosts for route id=rt-0a1b2c; triggering fallback policy" - decision-engine (2026-02-28T22:12:05Z): INFO fallback: "selected fallback variant=redwood-small-v1 region=us-east-1 cost_penalty=0.24 latency_est=120ms" - edge-proxy (2026-02-28T22:12:07Z): ERROR request-handler: "upstream connect error or disconnect before headers" COMMANDS I RAN / OUTPUTS (copy-paste friendly): - quick healthcheck against one of the failing backends: curl -v http://10.20.5.12:8080/health * Connected to 10.20.5.12 (10.20.5.12) port 8080 (#0) > GET /health HTTP/1.1 > Host: 10.20.5.12 < HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable < content-type: text/plain < retry-after: 10 < backend: overloaded / LB draining - route-manager debug: rictl routes get rt-0a1b2c --verbose --- route id: rt-0a1b2c origin: us-west-2 active_backends: 2/5 healthy fallback_policy: "regional-prefer-local, cross-region if none healthy" last_fallback_timestamp: 2026-02-28T22:12:05Z - list backend pool for us-west-2: rictl backends list --region us-west-2 --pool serving-pool-1 backend 10.20.5.12 status=UNHEALTHY last_probe=2026-02-28T22:11:32Z reason=503 backend 10.20.5.13 status=UNHEALTHY last_probe=2026-02-28T22:11:35Z reason=timeout backend 10.20.5.14 status=HEALTHY last_probe=2026-02-28T22:10:58Z - k8s logs for route-manager: kubectl -n routing logs route-manager-5f6d7 --since=15m [22:12:00] WARN no healthy hosts for route rt-0a1b2c [22:12:01] INFO falling back to cross-region variant redwood-small-v1@us-east-1 HYPOTHESES CONSIDERED (ordered roughly by likelihood): 1) Backend overload during a tight traffic surge + degraded autoscaling (some pods in the us-west-2 pool were stuck in terminating state). 2) New healthcheck regression from recent deploy that made the health endpoint return 503 intermittently. 3) Network level (NLB) flapping or intermittent drop between routing layer and serving nodes in us-west-2. 4) Control-plane race: routing decisions cached an old backend set that was partially removed, leading to transient "no healthy hosts" results. 5) Model-side resource starvation (KV cache thrashing) causing health endpoints to reject. WHAT I VERIFIED / EVIDENCE: - checked k8s events for nodes and pods in us-west-2: saw multiple pod terminations around 21:58-22:05 UTC (autoscaler activity). - checked last deploys: no route-manager deploys in last 48h; there was a serving-side deploy to serving-pool-1 6h before incident but metrics were stable until surge. - NLB metrics (Cloud provider): small spike in target 5xx and increased target health check latency; some targets marked Unhealthy within a 60s window. - autoscaler logs: some scale-up requests were throttled due to quota bumps delay (limiting factor). MITIGATION STEPS APPLIED (chronological): 1) Scoped traffic: temporarily changed route fallback policy to prefer local warm pool and not immediately cross-region (rictl routes update rt-0a1b2c --set fallback_policy=prefer-local-only --reason "mitigate cross-region flapping"). 2) Restarted route-manager and route-proxy pods in us-west-2 to pick up current backend set (kubectl rollout restart). 3) Manually drained one suspect backend (10.20.5.13) and rotated it out of the pool. 4) Requested emergency quota bump for nodes in us-west-2 to allow faster autoscale (eng-infra). 5) Added a temporary bypass to prefer healthy warm-pool instances (which are pre-warmed and avoid spinning up new pods). OUTCOME / POST-MITIGATION SIGNALS: - within ~10–15 minutes after steps 1–3, the 5xx rate dropped from 8% to ~0.6% and end-to-end latencies returned closer to baseline. - fallback to cross-region back to normal levels after backends recovered. - incident closed as mitigated at 14:42 local time. OPEN ACTIONS / TODOs (short-term ops): - (P0) Add more robust pre-warm/warm-pool capacity for serving-pool-1 in us-west-2 to reduce cold-start/fallback pressure. - (P0) Tweak fallback policy defaults: add hysteresis so we avoid immediate cross-region fallback on transient 1–2 probe failures. - (P1) Add a dashboard showing per-route fallback rate and cross-region fallback counts (help CS/SEs triage). - (P1) Improve autoscaler logging and alerting for throttled scale-up attempts. - (P2) Rewrite the healthcheck handler to return more diagnostic info (basic load factor) to aid future debugging. - (P2) Draft runbook for smart-routing regional failover with checklist of commands and who to ping. NOTES FOR POSTMORTEM: - root cause likely a combination: transient backend overload (scale-up lag) + conservative fallback policy that opted for immediate cross-region fallback rather than using local warm pool. - we should quantify how frequently fallbacks lead to cross-region traffic and the cost/latency impact (cost column in Optimize). RANDOM DEBUG TIPS / COMMANDS TO KEEP HANDY: - rictl backends list --region --pool

--verbose (shows last_probe and probe results) - rictl routes get --include-fallback-history - kubectl -n routing logs route-manager --since=30m | rg "fallback|no healthy|probe" - curl -v $BACKEND_IP:8080/health to verify probe response headers (look for retry-after / load hints) PERSONAL NOTES / RANT (scratchpad): - The policy of immediate cross-region fallback is safe for availability but noisy for latency/cost — we keep running into the tradeoff. We need a middle ground: prefer local warm pools, use cross-region only after X seconds/failed_probes and allow a short period of "graceful retry" to avoid flip-flopping. - Need to coordinate with infra teams earlier when we see autoscaler throttle signals — those are low-signal in the product dashboards today. REFERENCES / LINKS: see linked_artifacts at top. Also ping @Olivia and @Ethan for details on warm-pool capacity and quota bump timeline. END.
